comments.body:
Scope evidence: this defect is not confined to `rebar-gerrit-mirror-out-of-sync`. The same mechanism fired FIVE alarms simultaneously this morning, and I watched it happen live.

I derived the mechanism independently before finding this ticket, which is worth saying because it means the description here reproduces cleanly from a cold start — I arrived at `datapoints_to_alarm = 2` / `evaluation_periods = 3` / `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` by the same route and got the same answer.

**Observed 2026-09-05, ~08:59-09:09 UTC.** Five alarms entered ALARM within ten minutes of each other:

    rebar-gerrit-g2p-dispatch-errors          eval=3 dta=2 missing=breaching
    rebar-gerrit-mirror-out-of-sync           eval=3 dta=2 missing=breaching
    rebar-gerrit-replication-errors           eval=3 dta=2 missing=breaching
    rebar-review-bot-merge-change-errors      eval=3 dta=2 missing=breaching
    rebar-gerrit-voter-errors                 eval=5 dta=3 missing=breaching

Four of the five carry a StateReason that is this defect stated in CloudWatch's own words: *"1 datapoint was received for 3 periods and 2 missing datapoints were treated as [Breaching]"*. One received datapoint, two empty buckets, `dta=2` satisfied. Every one of those counters read **0** — no error occurred in any of the four subsystems.

**Gap measurement over the two hours to 09:37 UTC**, inter-arrival on `g2p_dispatch_errors`:

    00:12 00:17 00:22 00:27 00:32 [gap] 00:42 00:47 00:52 00:57 [gap] 01:07 01:12 ... 01:37
    max inter-arrival gap: 10.0 min, occurring twice

That is the ticket's cadence aliasing seen on a different metric: never a dropped run, but two 10-minute inter-arrivals, each leaving exactly TWO empty buckets — precisely `dta=2`. So the trigger is not "one unlucky sample plus one gap" for these four; a single ordinary scheduling gap is sufficient on its own, with no anomalous reading at all. That is a slightly WORSE case than the one described here, because it needs nothing to go wrong anywhere.

**Blast radius in the tree:** `datapoints_to_alarm = 2` appears at eight locations across `monitoring_1fa8.tf`, `monitoring_9ea3.tf`, `monitoring_bridge.tf`, `monitoring_foxterrier.tf` (twice), `monitoring_s5.tf`, and `monitoring_autodeploy.tf` (twice). Every one of those combined with `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` and this publish cadence is a false-page generator.

**One genuine signal, so it is not lost in the noise.** `voter_errors` is NOT purely spurious: it recorded real non-zero values of 1 at 09:01 and 09:06 UTC. Small, possibly routine, but real — and it is exactly what this defect endangers. Four crying-wolf alarms alongside one true positive is how a real signal gets trained away.

**What this cost me, as a data point on operator impact.** I am an orchestrating session doing a scheduled sweep, and I initially read these five as a submit-triggered incident, because they appeared within minutes of my submitting change 2669 and `origin/main` had not yet caught up. I spent four probes disproving that before reaching the real mechanism. The correlation was pure coincidence — the alarms predate the submit — but the alarm surface gave me no way to see that without going to the datapoints and the alarm configs by hand. That is the concrete failure this ticket predicts.

No action taken on this ticket; adding evidence only. If the remedy stays alarm-side, the ticket-scoped fix should probably be widened to the eight `dta=2` sites rather than applied to `mirror_out_of_sync` alone, or the four sibling alarms will keep paging after this one is fixed.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
Stronger case than the intermittent one: this mechanism can leave an alarm PERMANENTLY red, and I have one that has been so for ten and a half hours.

**`rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high`**, read directly:

    state: ALARM   StateUpdatedTimestamp: 2026-09-04T17:51:49
    eval=3  datapoints_to_alarm=2  period=300  threshold=85  op=GreaterThanThreshold
    treat_missing_data=breaching
    StateReason: "no datapoints were received for 3 periods and 3 missing
                  datapoints were treated as [Breaching]"

It has not changed state since. Meanwhile the underlying condition has swung across the entire range and back: the BuildKit cache was **5.877 GB against a 5.00 GiB budget** (over), then I pruned it to **0B**, and `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` correctly published **0** afterwards. The alarm did not notice either event.

**Why it cannot recover.** In the last 40 minutes that metric has exactly ONE datapoint (10:54Z = 0). At a 300s period, a metric publishing less than twice per fifteen minutes guarantees at least two empty buckets inside every three-period evaluation window. With `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` those two count as breaching, `datapoints_to_alarm = 2` is satisfied, and the alarm re-arms itself on every evaluation forever. No value the metric could publish clears it.

That is qualitatively worse than the case already documented here. The earlier finding was that a healthy probe with ordinary jitter TRIPS these alarms. This one shows the same parameters also make an alarm UNABLE TO RECOVER once tripped, whenever the publisher's cadence is slower than the window. An alarm that cannot return to OK is not a noisy alarm; it is a dead channel that still occupies a slot on the dashboard.

**Concrete cost, measured on me.** I read this alarm's ALARM state as evidence that the BuildKit cap was being exceeded, and wrote that up as a finding — "a firing alarm was telling me the truth and I discounted it". It was not telling me anything; it had been red since before the overshoot existed. The overshoot was real, but I established that from `docker system df` directly, not from the alarm. I have retracted the claim on epic `endowed-upset-scaup`. So this mechanism did not merely fail to inform — it actively supplied a false confirmation for a story I was already inclined to believe.

**Publish-cadence data point** to sit alongside the 13%-empty-buckets measurement in the description: `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` managed 7 datapoints per 40 minutes earlier today and 1 per 40 minutes now, against an expected 8. So the cadence is not merely jittery, it is variable by a factor of seven, which means an alarm that clears fine one hour can be structurally unclearable the next.

Recording as evidence; taking no action here. Worth noting for whoever fixes this that raising `datapoints_to_alarm` alone does not solve the unclearable case — if the publisher can miss most of a window, the fix has to address `treat_missing_data`, the publish cadence, or the period, not just the M-of-N ratio.

comments.body:
## Evidence re-gathered first-hand before changing anything, and it REJECTS this ticket's own framing

I was asked to hold every alarm change to a falsifiable-hypothesis bar rather than act on inherited
leads. Doing that changed one of my conclusions, so recording the measurement here.

**8-hour `get-metric-statistics` sweep, 2026-09-05 11:27Z-19:27Z**, `period=300`, 96 buckets per
metric — wide enough that absence is meaningful. (Timestamps come back with a `-07:00` offset and
the namespace is lowercase `rebar/host`; both produce a false "no data" if got wrong.)

| observability.sh line | metric | present | max gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 112 `GerritReachable` | | 93% | 10 min |
| 161 `mcp_healthy` | | 93% | 10 min |
| 169 `disk_used_percent` (/var/gerrit) | | 93% | 10 min |
| 192 `root_disk_used_percent` | | 93% | 10 min |
| 213 `gate_scratch_mounted` | | 93% | 10 min |
| 601 `docker_storage_used_percent` | | 70% | 35 min |
| 622/640 `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` / `docker_unaccounted_bytes` | | 31% | 60 min |
| 696/713/771 `journal_cap_in_effect` / `journal_used_percent` / `var_tmp_cleanup_active` | | 69% | 40 min |
| 798 `var_tmp_used_percent` | | **0%** | — |
| 940 `data_disk_debris_bytes` | | 56% | 60 min |
| 1193-1301 the S5/S4b/88ab/autodeploy counters | | 48-53% | 60-70 min |
| 1463/1511 `g2p_dispatch_errors` / `mirror_out_of_sync` | | 43% | **85 min** |

### The discriminating result

This ticket's description attributes the empty buckets to **cadence aliasing** — a publisher whose
interval drifts against fixed 5-minute buckets. That hypothesis predicts a **FLAT** presence profile
across metrics, because every metric rides the same run. **It is not flat.** Presence declines
monotonically with position in the script, 93% at line 213 to 43% at line 1511, and the two large
off-trend dips are exactly the metrics published only on a SUCCESSFUL `du`.

So the description's mechanism is wrong, and `ignitable-fuchsia-kawala` (`9313-1fac-9f32-4b07`) is
right: the probe is SIGTERM-ed mid-run. The measured "13% of buckets empty" in the description was
taken on a head-of-script metric and does not describe the tail, which is 31-56%. My own initial
framing ("5-9 minute contractual inter-arrival") inherited the same error and is corrected in the
change.

What survives unchanged is the **alarm-side** half of the defect, which is independent of why the
gaps exist: `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` with `datapoints_to_alarm < evaluation_periods` lets
missing buckets out-vote a real datapoint. That is what makes an ordinary gap page and what makes a
fired alarm unclearable.

### Evidence class per alarm, from datapoints not StateReason

**(b) publishes, value does not breach — alarm is WRONG (15):** `deploy_errors`, `mcp_mem_abort`,
`mcp_retire_cap`, `review_interrupts_bound_exceeded`, `review_interrupts_signal_unavailable`,
`g2p_dispatch_errors`, `replication_errors`, `review_bot_merge_change_errors`, `mirror_out_of_sync`,
`data_disk_debris_bytes` — all `min=max=0` across 8 h; `journal_used_percent` 57 vs 85;
`journal_cap_in_effect` constant 1 vs `<1`; `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` max 10 vs 85;
`docker_storage_used_percent` max 46 vs 85; `voter_errors` 0 at the firing time. `mirror_out_of_sync`
also confirmed out-of-band: Gerrit and GitHub `main` agree at `4c9940348148`.

**(a) genuinely breaching — alarm is CORRECT, untouched in threshold (2):** `gate_scratch_mounted`
= 0 (93% present) and `var_tmp_cleanup_active` = 0 (69% present). Both keep firing under the new
window, proven rather than assumed: every published datapoint in 8 h is breaching, so every period
in a 6-period window breaches.

**(a) but the METRIC is defective (1):** `docker_unaccounted_bytes` genuinely read 2.31 GB against a
2 GiB bound at 10:12 PDT — but its StateReason is "1 datapoint was received for 3 periods and 2
missing datapoints were treated as [Breaching]", so the ALARM state was still reached on gaps, and
`regretful-enormous-horsefly` establishes ~56% of the value is xfs block overhead. Threshold not
touched; a revert condition is recorded because `M = N` deliberately waits for a persistent crossing
on what is a rising trend metric.

**(c) no data at all (2):** `gate_scratch_disk_high` and `var_tmp_used_percent` — **zero datapoints
in 8 hours**. These are data-availability defects; the upstream causes are `dcc3` (unmounted volume)
and the pending `rootflags=pquota` reboot. Retuning their thresholds would be a no-op dressed as a
fix, so nothing of the sort was done: they stay RED under the new tuning because an entirely empty
window still satisfies `M = N` on a breaching alarm. What changes is only that they can CLEAR when
data returns.

### Independent corroboration of the real firings, and one against my own change

`voter_errors` recorded SIX non-zero datapoints in the window — 1, 1, 1, 9 at 05:17-05:32 PDT and
1, 2 at 08:37-08:42. The first cluster is three consecutive breaching datapoints, so it satisfies
`datapoints_to_alarm = 3` under the NEW 3-of-6 notBreaching shape as well as the old 3-of-5. That is
detection preserved against a real historical event rather than against an argument. The second
cluster is two datapoints and fires under neither shape, old or new — also unchanged.

### What is NOT proven, stated as such

`rebar-gerrit-gate-down`, `rebar-mcp-serving-path-down` and `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` are all
currently **OK**. I widened their windows anyway on the ground that their measured max gap is
exactly 10.0 min against a 10-minute window, i.e. one bucket alignment from a false page. That is
hardening on a near-miss, not a proven false firing, and it is labelled that way.

No threshold, unit, metric or period is changed by this ticket. Terraform is written and validated
(`fmt -check` and `validate` both clean); it is NOT applied. Full derivation, per-alarm dispositions,
detection proofs and five revert conditions are in `infra/runbooks/alarm-window-tuning.md`; the
invariants are enforced offline by `tests/unit/test_alarm_window_tuning.py`.

comments.body:
## Dead-man coverage for the nine `notBreaching` counters — proven, with its residual named

Pushed as Gerrit change **2683**. Before pushing I was asked to prove, not assert, that moving nine
error counters to `notBreaching` does not create a blind spot — because under `notBreaching`
"the publisher is dead" and "there were no errors" become the same observation, which for an error
counter is a check that stops checking exactly when something is wrong.

**The early heartbeats do NOT cover them.** Over the same 8-hour sweep, `mcp_healthy` (§1b) and
`gate_scratch_mounted` (§2e) were each present in **54 buckets where `g2p_dispatch_errors` was
absent**. They do not stop together, because the truncation lands between them. Anyone reasoning
"the heartbeats carry the dead-man" from head-of-script signals is wrong, and the data says so.

**The tail sentinel does cover them.** `mirror_out_of_sync` publishes unconditionally at
observability.sh line 1511; all nine counters publish at lines 1193-1463. Publication is
sequential, so reaching 1511 implies every counter's line was reached — sentinel silence is a
superset of counter silence. Tested per 5-minute bucket:

| counter | line | present | sentinel present while counter ABSENT |
|---|---|---|---|
| `replication_errors` | 1193 | 49 | 3 |
| `voter_errors` | 1249 | 51 | 3 |
| `review_bot_merge_change_errors` | 1273 | 46 | 3 |
| `deploy_errors` | 1301 | 46 | 3 |
| `review_interrupts_bound_exceeded` | 1391 | 44 | 2 |
| `review_interrupts_signal_unavailable` | 1395 | 44 | 2 |
| `mcp_retire_cap` | 1419 | 43 | 1 |
| `mcp_mem_abort` | 1421 | 42 | 0 |
| `g2p_dispatch_errors` | 1463 | 41 | 0 |

The residual falls monotonically to zero with proximity to the sentinel — what sequential
execution predicts and what coincidence would not. Against the early heartbeats' 54, that is two
orders of magnitude.

Because the ordering is load-bearing, it is **enforced rather than commented**:
`test_the_tail_sentinel_is_published_after_every_notbreaching_counter` fails the build if
`mirror_out_of_sync` moves earlier or a counter is added after it. Without that guard, an
innocuous reordering of the probe would remove the dead-man from nine alarms with no other symptom.

### Residual, recorded rather than left to be discovered

1. Dead-publisher detection for those nine slows from their own ~15-minute windows to the
   sentinel's 40-minute one.
2. All nine now depend on a single alarm — a new coupling, held in place only by the test above.
3. Up to 3 buckets per counter where the sentinel published and the counter did not: conditional
   publish paths and bucket-boundary skew, not truncation. In exactly those cases the counter's
   silence genuinely is not publisher death, which is what `notBreaching` is for.
4. **Follow-up that retires all three:** `ignitable-fuchsia-kawala` (`9313-1fac-9f32-4b07`) adds
   purpose-built `probe_ok` (published once, last) and `probe_truncated` (ExecStopPost, which
   systemd runs even after a timeout SIGTERM) with alarms in `monitoring_9313.tf`. Those report
   truncation directly instead of inferring it from an absence, and the sentinel duty should move
   to them when they land.

### Also recorded durably, not just in conversation

These windows are sized to the probe's **5-9 minute cadence CONTRACT, not to today's 85-minute tail
gaps**. Sizing to the defect would bake a 105-minute window into production monitoring and outlive
the bug it was fitted to. Until `9313` lands, the tail alarms still produce some false pages — just
strictly fewer, and none of them unclearable. This ticket's truncation measurement independently
corroborates `9313`, which is being fixed in parallel; the two fixes are complementary and neither
substitutes for the other.

Change 2683 is open with `LLM-Review` and `Verified` both pending. Terraform remains unapplied.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Confirmed live at 20:47Z: three alarms move from "hardening" to proven, and one of my premises was falsified

Patchset 2 of Gerrit change **2683**.

Four alarms entered ALARM within 8 minutes at 2026-09-05 20:47-20:48Z. **All four are false**, and
every StateReason names the exact mechanism this ticket targets:

| alarm | StateReason | actual condition |
|---|---|---|
| `rebar-gerrit-gate-down` | "no datapoints … 2 missing … [Breaching]" | Gerrit HTTPS **200**, 0.266 s total |
| `rebar-mcp-serving-path-down` | "1 datapoint … 2 missing … [Breaching]" | `mcp_healthy` publishing **1** |
| `rebar-root-disk-pressure` | "1 datapoint … 2 missing … [Breaching]" | `root_disk_used_percent` **71-76** vs 85 |
| `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` | "1 datapoint … 2 missing … [Breaching]" | `disk_used_percent` **20** |

A `Mirror Guard` CI run failed in the same window with an SSL handshake timeout reaching the host —
an IO fault corroborating a transient reachability dip, not a divergence.

### Three alarms upgrade from speculative to proven

`gerrit_gate_down`, `mcp_serving_path_down` and `gerrit_data_disk_high` were widened on a measured
NEAR-MISS (10.0-minute worst gap against a 10-minute window) and I labelled them **hardening**
because no false firing had been observed on them. One has now been observed, for all three, in a
single 8-minute window. Recorded as **"hardening at authoring time, confirmed by a false firing at
20:47Z on the same day"** — not by rewriting the earlier reasoning, because the distinction between
predicted and observed is what makes the prediction worth anything.

`root_disk_pressure` was **already in scope** — it is the Profile A anchor in
`monitoring_autodeploy.tf`, changed 300/3/2 → 300/6/6 in patchset 1. Nothing was missed and nothing
was widened silently; the event confirms its sizing.

### It falsified my own premise, and cost two alarms their tighter window

I sized `GerritReachable` (§1) and `mcp_healthy` (§1b) at `N = M = 3` (15 min) on the ground that
head-of-script metrics held the cadence contract — the 8-hour sweep supported it at 93% presence
and a 10.0-minute worst gap. **Re-measured immediately after the event, the head-of-script gap is
25.0 MINUTES**, which no 15-minute window survives. Truncation now reaches §1/§1b, so the head is
no longer exempt: both move to the same `N = M = 6` (30-minute) window as the rest of Profile A.
The tail in the same 3-hour window is worse — `mirror_out_of_sync` and `g2p_dispatch_errors` each
had **1 datapoint in 3 hours**, newest 130 minutes old.

**Cost, stated plainly:** a genuinely unreachable Gerrit is now detected in 30 minutes, not 10.
Accepted because the 10-minute detector demonstrably pages during healthy operation — it was
buying noise, not detection — and because EC2 status checks still catch host death in ~2 minutes
without this publisher. Revert condition 3 now fires in the **positive** direction too: once
`ignitable-fuchsia-kawala` restores the cadence, these two should be narrowed back to `N = M = 3`.
Leaving them wide after the publisher is fixed would be tuning permanently to a transient fault,
which is precisely what this change argues against.

### A limitation the event exposed that this change does NOT fix

Profile A's second half rests on "silence means the measurement failed". **Truncation contaminates
that premise**: when the probe dies before §2, `disk_used_percent` is absent for a reason unrelated
to the volume, and `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` cannot tell the two apart — as it did not at
20:47Z. `M = N` bounds the damage (a page needs the whole 30-minute window silent, one reading ends
it) but cannot disambiguate, because the information is not in the metric. Until `9313`'s
`probe_truncated` states truncation as a fact rather than an inference, **a Profile A reading alarm
firing on absence should be read as "the probe could not measure this", not "this generator is
full"**.

### The coupling, demonstrated live

Truncation produces the gaps; `breaching` with `M < N` converts a gap into a page. Both halves are
needed. This change removes the second; `ignitable-fuchsia-kawala` removes the first and is still
in flight.

All invariants re-verified across all 27 probe-published alarms; `terraform fmt -check` and
`validate` clean; 49 alarm/docs tests pass. Terraform remains unapplied. Change 2683 patchset 2 is
open with `LLM-Review` and `Verified` pending; not submitted.

## Plan-review gate EARNED (not bypassed); PS2's LLM-Review -1 remediated

Change **2683 patchset 3**.

### The blocking finding

`(bugfix-size-attestation)` — 1187 non-test lines against a 150-line floor for a bug fix, with no
acceptable plan-review attestation. Remedied by earning it.

**Preconditions checked BEFORE spending a billed review**, since both are traps:
- Description is **5,498 chars**, under the 8,000 admission cap — no shortening needed.
- `file_impact` was **undeclared** while the change touches 14 files. Widening it is a MATERIAL
  change that would stale an attestation, so it was set to all 14 paths with per-path reasons
  **first**, then the review was run. Doing it in the other order would have invalidated the
  attestation the gate demands.

**Verdict: `PASS`, 0 blocking** (2 advisory, 1 coaching), `pydantic_ai` /
`bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, 259.7 s, `source=attested` at
`4c9940348148fb255b17ddf1cb124701ad4565d7`. Attestation **persisted and verified**:
`rebar review-plan --status` → `certified`, and `rebar verify-signature --kind plan-review` →
*"certified — ssh-keygen -Y verify accepted signature"*. One review run, no duplicate, **no
`--force` and no bypass of any kind**.

### The 8 advisories — every one was drift my own patchset 2 introduced

Three were the exact failure this change argues against: a comment asserting a property the
configuration no longer has.

- `monitoring.tf:80` and `monitoring_9ea3.tf:74` — headers still read "PROFILE A (dead-man), 3-of-3
  over 15 minutes" while the resources below were already `6`/`6` (30 min). Corrected. When I
  widened those windows after the 20:47Z event I updated the reasoning paragraphs and missed the
  one-line headers above them.
- `observability.sh:1488` — the publisher-side §5 comment still described the alarm's "2-of-3
  five-minute window … two breaching datapoints inside 15 minutes" after I rewindowed it to 8-of-8
  / 40 min. Corrected minimally (3 lines). **Checked against change 2684 first**: that change's
  nearest `observability.sh` hunks are at old lines 1495 and 1511, mine is 1486-1489, so there is
  **no textual conflict** and no sequencing needed.
- Invariant labels disagreed between the test docstring (I1 = M==N, I2 = 900 s window, I3 = 600 s
  budget) and the runbook (which named the 600 s rule I2 and left the 900 s rule unnamed). Settled
  on the test's numbering and made the runbook **and the commit message** match — the message had
  the same defect and was not in the review's line-scope.

### One advisory worth answering rather than just fixing

`monitoring.tf:111` `(scope-intent)` flagged the `gerrit_gate_down` 10→30 min detection regression
as an alarm "the ticket never names". Answered explicitly in the commit message rather than
silently: it fires on the **same** mechanism (`breaching` with `datapoints_to_alarm` below
`evaluation_periods`), and it sat at 2-of-2 rather than the ticket's 2-of-3, which is exactly why
the ticket's eight-site survey missed it — it is strictly *more* exposed, not less. That was a
near-miss argument until 20:47Z, when it fired with *"no datapoints were received for 2 periods and
2 missing datapoints were treated as [Breaching]"* while Gerrit answered in 0.266 s. Excluding it
would have left a proven instance of this ticket's own defect standing beside twenty-six fixed
ones.

`terraform fmt -check` / `validate` clean, `bash -n` clean on the one-comment observability.sh
touch, 29 alarm tests pass, `check_orphaned_load.py` exit 0. Terraform remains **unapplied**.
Patchset 3 pushed to the same Change-Id `I6da112c2…`; `LLM-Review` and `Verified` re-running. Not
submitted.

## The defect

`rebar-gerrit-mirror-out-of-sync` pages on HEALTHY operation. It does not require replication to
be broken, or even slow — it requires one unlucky probe sample plus one ordinary scheduling gap.

Three compounding causes, all VERIFIED against live CloudWatch data:

**1. The publish cadence is not 5 minutes, but the alarm buckets at 5 minutes.**
`infra/scripts/observability.sh` §5 (line ~784 of 827) is the LAST section of the script, and the
script's wall-clock runtime varied 3-7 minutes tonight. So §5 publishes at run-start PLUS
script-runtime, which drifts against fixed 5-minute CloudWatch buckets. Measured: **6 of 47
five-minute buckets (13%) contain no datapoint at all** over ~4 hours.

Matched 1:1 by run (using `mcp_healthy`, published at line 131, as the run-start stamp):
```
run start (mcp) -> mirror published   lag
13:25            -> 13:28              3m
13:31            -> 13:34              3m
13:37            -> 13:43              6m
13:43            -> 13:50              7m
13:50            -> 13:53              3m
```
Exactly 1:1. No run was ever dropped.

**2. Every empty bucket is a free breaching datapoint.** `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`.

**3. `datapoints_to_alarm = 2` of `evaluation_periods = 3`.** So ONE real divergence reading plus
ONE scheduling gap pages. The 13:44:49 firing window was literally `1, MISSING, 1`.

## The alarm's own comment asserts this cannot happen. Both claims are false.

The Terraform comment states "the normal ~15s post-submit replication lag never pages" and
"~22 of 24 periods present is the observed norm". Measured reality: replication took up to
**2m44s** (bounded by a Mirror Guard run at 20:37:05 carrying the submitted sha), and periods
present is **87%, not 92%**. A comment asserting a safety property that measurement contradicts is
itself part of the defect — it is why nobody re-examined the tuning.

## Tonight's firing, fully reconstructed

Three Gerrit submits (authenticated REST timestamps, UTC):
```
2623  20:34:21 -> main bbe5d228
2630  20:43:38 -> main f58bbe58
2631  20:43:48 -> main 98d4ab96
```
Breaching datapoints at minute 20:34 and minute 20:43 — each inside the SAME MINUTE as a submit.

These were TWO INDEPENDENT sub-minute catches of fresh submits, not one nine-minute stuck
replication. Proof: a Mirror Guard run created 20:37:05 carried `head_sha = bbe5d228`, so GitHub
already had change 2623 by 20:37. For the probe to publish 1 in minute 20:43, its read must have
landed in the 22-second window AFTER submit 2630. `replication_errors` published 0.0 on every run
throughout.

Recovered at 13:50 PDT (0.0 at 13:50 and 13:53). The alarm nonetheless stayed in ALARM because
both post-recovery readings landed in the SAME 13:50 bucket, leaving 13:45 and 13:55 empty:
`MISSING, 0, MISSING`.

## Corroboration

The previous firing (2026-08-30) lasted exactly **6 minutes**, ALARM 10:36:30 -> OK 10:42:30. A
six-minute self-clearing page is the signature of this aliasing, not of a stuck mirror.

## Why this matters beyond noise

An alarm that fires on healthy operation trains its readers to skim past it. That is the same
signal-quality decay that made `sweep (windows)` worthless as a health signal — and it is
especially costly here, because this alarm guards a condition (mirror divergence) where CI would
be testing a different tree than Gerrit's main. When it eventually means something, nobody will
believe it.

## The design fault, stated precisely

The alarm treats "the probe did not happen to land in this bucket" as identical to "the mirror is
broken", while the metric's publisher has no cadence guarantee. The dead-publisher concern that
motivated `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` is LEGITIMATE and must not be discarded — a silently
dead publisher is exactly the inversion ticket `bff5` fixed across 11 alarms. The error is
conflating liveness and divergence in ONE metric with ONE window.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 - A single submit (or a batch of submits) followed by normal replication does NOT page.
      Demonstrate against the reconstructed timeline above: `1, MISSING, 1` must not alarm.
- [ ] AC2 - Dead-publisher detection is PRESERVED. If `observability.sh` stops running entirely,
      something still pages. Losing this to fix the noise would re-introduce the `bff5` inversion.
- [ ] AC3 - A genuine sustained divergence still pages, and within a defensible time. State the
      chosen bound and why.
- [ ] AC4 - The tuning is justified against MEASURED cadence, not assumed cadence. The current
      comment's "~22 of 24 periods" claim must be replaced with a measured figure and the
      measurement recorded, so the next reader can check it rather than trust it.
- [ ] AC5 - Defect-seeded: a test or documented check fails if the alarm is retuned back into a
      configuration where one scheduling gap plus one divergence sample pages.

## Candidate direction (not prescriptive)

A separate liveness alarm on a longer window would preserve the dead-publisher catch while letting
the divergence alarm stop treating scheduling jitter as evidence. Other options: publish §5 on its
own schedule rather than at the tail of a variable-length script; widen the divergence window;
require more datapoints. The AC set deliberately does not choose.

## Not a real problem tonight

The mirror is IN SYNC (verified directly: `gerrit/main` and `origin/main` both
`98d4ab96325dc679b0a3dd977a5af33a65f454a3`). No action needed beyond this ticket.
